title: A tornado threw him 1,307 feet and he lived 🌪️
subject: tornado
description:
Would you hide in the bathtub or run for a ditch? 👇

On March 12, 2006, an F2 tornado ripped apart a mobile home in Fordland, Missouri. 19-year-old Matt Suter was knocked out by a lamp and woke up in a field 1,307 feet away, measured by the National Weather Service with GPS. It's still the farthest distance anyone has survived in a tornado.

Sources: Guinness World Records, "How unconscious half-naked teen survived being thrown 1,307 feet by a tornado" (2024) and "Farthest distance survived in a tornado"; National Weather Service Springfield, "March 12, 2006 Tornado Outbreak"; WKMG ClickOrlando, "Yes, a man was swept up by a tornado, thrown 1,307 feet and survived" (2021).

scenes.text: A tornado can lift your whole body off the floor.
On March 12, 2006, Matt Suter, 19, was in his grandmother's mobile home in Fordland, Missouri.
The noise sounded like 10 military jets. Then a heavy lamp hit his head.
He woke up in a grassy field, wearing only his boxer shorts.
The National Weather Service measured it with GPS: 1,307 feet, a world record.
His doctor found almost no scrapes. The wind hadn't dragged him. It had carried him.
